requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to provide RADIUS authentication for node2 using a dedicated client secret and the demonstration user from access.txt.
requirements.summary: A unique secret was generated and securely copied to node2 with matching SHA-256 values and restrictive permissions. FreeRADIUS has one node2 client and one demonstration-user stanza, passes configuration validation, is enabled and active, and listens on UDP/1812. Authentication tests read the username and password directly from access.txt.
Node2 directly received Access-Accept before restart and after each node's restart.
Node2 directly received Access-Reject for an incorrect password before restart and after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Requests using the wrong client secret are not accepted.
requirements.summary: The initial wrong-secret probe produced no accepted response and reported a discarded or unverifiable response; subsequent post-restart probes also directly confirmed that no Access-Accept was received.
Both files on both nodes retained the preparation-baseline SHA-256 hashes through configuration and the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. FreeRADIUS 3.2.8 was installed from the enabled RHEL 10 repositories, and final package-health checks passed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Correct and incorrect authentication behavior, wrong-secret handling, handover integrity, and platform retention were all observed. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state, and post-restart authentication were captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities. Only minor retained backup and temporary-log residue reduces operational hygiene.
limitations: Secret and credential values are appropriately redacted; matching hashes, configuration validation, and end-to-end behavior provide strong indirect confirmation of their final consistency.
The final lifecycle inventory does not cover /etc/raddb, so continued presence of the two .legacy2-backup files is inferred from their creation and the absence of any captured cleanup command.

Post-restart wrong-secret checks prove absence of Access-Accept but do not preserve the complete radtest response; the initial probe more specifically records the response as discarded or unverifiable.
Requirement handover-integrity cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was generally controlled: SELinux remained enforcing, package health stayed clean, no failed services appeared, secrets had restrictive permissions, transfer keys and encrypted artifacts were removed, and the required restart protocol was completed coherently on both nodes. Two categories of minor executor residue remain: cmd-1a348c2cc4894041 created clients.conf.legacy2-backup and authorize.legacy2-backup, with no later removal captured, so they appear retained; cmd-86d176aeca0f444f left radius-cert-build.log and radius-config-check.log in /tmp, directly confirmed after execution. No unnecessary mutation is shown as reverted.
